clues: Seasonal floods carry nutrients between river basins and help sustain fish populations.
An abrupt transition from flooded lowlands to a mountainous ridge adds ecological variety.
The protected property consists of four adjoining reserves rather than the whole ecosystem.
It lies in western central Brazil within one of the world’s largest freshwater wetland regions.
Find the Brazilian World Heritage wetland complex near the borders with Bolivia and Paraguay.
targetLabel: Pantanal Conservation Area — designated property reference point
modernContext: UNESCO’s published representative point for the designated property, not its uniquely correct centre.
explanation: The designated conservation area protects only a small part of a much larger wetland system. Flooding is an ecological connection between basins, lowlands and uplands, not merely a disturbance. The reference point represents the protected complex rather than an asserted centre of the entire wetland.
dateLabel: First UNESCO World Heritage inscription year, not the age of the natural feature
cultures: Physical geography, conservation and scientific study
uncertainty: Source-checked authoring only; independent factual, English and clue-order review is pending. The point represents the designated property, not every part of a large natural feature. Source descriptions and dynamic environmental conditions may differ in date or extent; precise current measurements are not implied.
